event_station_013@node_spine_2.quirk: Their transport tank sloshes with each gesture.

event_station_013@node_branch_1_beta_0.quirk: One of their servos hums a note. It is not a musical note. It is trying.

event_station_012@node_branch_1_beta_0.quirk: Their outline is perfectly clear except in your peripheral vision, where it declines to commit.

shipLog.text: ◆ At each stop, STOP opens the Stop menu: the things you can do here. Each verb costs time and the crew's effort, which costs morale. RESUME flies on to the next stop.
◆ Crop planted. MARV notes this is the point of no return. The mission now depends on something that needs water and doesn't respond to reason.
Arrived: The Marginal Improvement. The leg cost −3 FUEL, +2 MORALE, −2 FOOD, −2 H2O, −1 O2, 7 DAYS. Filed.
The Paperwork. The captain chose “Sign everything without reading”. Noted.
You signed. +5 MORALE, 1 DAY. It will not last.
◆ Materials aboard. The FABRICATOR (Stop menu) turns them into hull patches, repair kits and the rest; a print takes days and adds wear. A station's FAB SERVICE resets the wear.
Arrived: Fort Probably Fine. The leg cost −3 FUEL, −3 FOOD, −3 H2O, −1 O2, 8 DAYS. Filed.
◆ A tomato has fallen off the vine. Three crew members have opinions about this. (−2 morale)
The Half-Built Relay. The captain chose “Give them the time”. Noted.
Your ship holds the girder steady while their welders walk the seam. +5 FUEL, +4 MORALE, 4 DAYS. It will not last.
Market Row. The captain chose “BACK TO DOCK”. Noted.
1 DAY. It will not last.
Station Inbound. The captain chose “LEAVE STATION”. Noted.
Nothing aboard changed. It will not last.
◆ The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Safe burns out there, captain. The ring'll still be here next pass.”
◆ Docked. The dock has rooms to visit and the Market Row. From the Stop menu: MEDBAY heals everyone, DRYDOCK patches the hull, FAB SERVICE resets the fabricator. Waving off closes all of them.
Arrived: Planet McPlanetface. The leg cost −3 FUEL, +2 MORALE, −2 FOOD, −2 H2O, −1 O2, 7 DAYS. Filed.
◆ Soil sampler survey logged (1/3). The colony office will want this.
Spots on the Leaves. The captain chose “Keep an eye on it”. Noted.
You make a note of it and leave the plants alone. 1 DAY. It will not last.
◆ INV opens the hold. Each item says what it does and which events it can open. USE it from there, SELL it when docked, or JETTISON it to free a slot.
Tomato: VEGETATIVE. 32% grown, health 90. Temporarily.
Arrived: Nebula 4. The leg cost −3 FUEL, −3 FOOD, −3 H2O, −5 CROP, +2 MORALE, −1 O2, 8 DAYS. Filed.
◆ The ship computer notes that more events have been logged about the tomatoes than about the hull. It does not editorialize. (−5 crop health)
The Galley Has a Ghost. The captain chose “Confine them until the next stop”. Noted.
You assign them a cabin and a door that locks from outside. −4 MORALE, 1 DAY. As calculated.
◆ A fork ahead. The route labels are not decoration: each one leans its branch toward that kind of stop and that kind of event.
Arrived: Route Decision. The leg cost −3 FUEL, +2 MORALE, −2 FOOD, −2 H2O, −1 O2, 7 DAYS. Filed.
Both Lanes Watched. The captain chose “Run the storm: starboard lane”. Noted.
You take the storm. −10 HULL, −2 MORALE, 1 DAY. As calculated.
◆ The readout strip opens Orders: pace trades speed for fuel and morale, rations trade food for morale, and the water split shares water between the crew and the crop.
Arrived: Meridian Stopgap. The leg cost −3 FUEL, −3 FOOD, −3 H2O, +2 MORALE, −1 O2, 8 DAYS. Filed.
Station Inbound. The captain chose “LEAVE STATION”. Noted.
Nothing aboard changed. It will not last.
◆ The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Safe burns out there, captain. The ring'll still be here next pass.”
◆ The crop card opens the growbay: its health, its water, its threats, who tends it, TREAT for pests, and the harvest.
Tomato: FLOWERING. 59% grown, health 97. Temporarily.

identity.name: Ines Vahl
identity.story: They map places for a survey office that stopped paying them two years ago. They kept mapping. They stowed away because your route crosses three sectors whose charts they know to be wrong, and being aboard a ship headed into a known error was, professionally speaking, irresistible.
identity.line: Your nav charts are wrong at marker sixty-one. Charmingly wrong. Fatally wrong. May I see the helm?
identity.join_note: Draws corrections directly onto official charts in pen. The pen is the statement.
